title: Bernadette at Lourdes (1858)
hook: a sick, poor, fourteen-year-old sees a lady in a grotto and digs where a spring appears
carry: she was only asked to tell

segments.voice: Yesterday, Thomas More, who refused an oath in silence. Your line was the king's good servant, God's first. Did you keep your quiet promise? This week, the modern saints. Day ninety-two.

February 1858, a small town in the foothills of the Pyrenees. It's cold. A girl of fourteen goes out with her sister and a friend to gather firewood and bones to sell. She's small for her age, she has asthma, and she can't read. Her family is so poor they're living in one damp room that used to be the town jail. The other two cross a stream. She hesitates at the cold water, near a rocky hollow in the cliff called Massabielle. Then she hears a sound like wind, looks up, and sees, in the grotto, a young lady dressed in white, smiling at her. Today: Bernadette at Lourdes.
screen: `FEBRUARY 1858.` → `A GIRL GATHERING WOOD.` → `A LADY IN THE GROTTO.`

segments.voice: Her name was Bernadette Soubirous. Over that spring and summer she said the lady appeared to her eighteen times. Crowds began to follow her to the grotto. They saw nothing but a girl kneeling, her face changed. Then, on one of the visits, Bernadette said the lady told her to drink from the spring and wash in it. There was no spring. So she scratched at the muddy ground with her hands, and tried to drink the dirty water, and smeared her face. People thought she'd lost her mind. But over the next days, water began to flow from that spot, and it still flows. Weeks later, she asked the lady her name. The answer came in the local dialect, in words Bernadette didn't understand: I am the Immaculate Conception. She repeated them all the way to the parish priest so she wouldn't forget. He went pale. That title for Mary had been defined by the Pope only four years before, and he doubted this girl had ever heard it. The police questioned her, and so did the clergy. She never changed her story, and she never tried to convince anyone. She said, in effect, that her job was to tell, not to make people believe. She later became a nun, suffered long illness, and died at thirty-five. Catholics call apparitions like this private revelation: the Church approved Lourdes, but no Catholic is required to believe it. Millions go anyway, many of them sick, to bathe in the water and to pray.
screen: `EIGHTEEN VISITS TO THE GROTTO.` · `SHE DUG, AND A SPRING CAME.` · `I AM THE IMMACULATE CONCEPTION.` · `ASKED TO TELL, NOT TO CONVINCE.` · then: `A PLACE FOR THE SICK.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold someone who is ill. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one person who is sick right now, in body or in mind. See their face. Picture them the way pilgrims picture the ones they carry to Lourdes: not fixed, just held, just brought. If you pray, you can pray for them now, maybe with a Hail Mary. If you don't, simply hold them in your attention and wish them well. The bell holds the time.
Bernadette at Lourdes. A poor, sick girl who saw a lady in a grotto, dug for a spring, and only ever told what she saw. Today's word.
Your line: she was only asked to tell. Today, say one true thing plainly, and let it go. You don't have to win the argument. Day ninety-two.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the feast of Our Lady of Lourdes on February 11, also the World Day of the Sick; millions of pilgrims visit the grotto each year, many of them ill, to pray, join the candlelight processions and bathe in the spring water.

original.note: the lady's words in Bernadette's local Gascon dialect (not Latin, not French): I am the Immaculate Conception.

trapdoor: what you thought: a miracle spring in France.
what it means: a poor girl who saw a lady, dug where she was told, and only ever told what she saw.
what a scholar hears: the lady spoke Gascon, not French, and named herself with a title the Pope had defined in 1854, four years earlier.

notes: Bernadette born January 7, 1844; aged 14 at the first apparition (February 11, 1858); died April 16, 1879 at 35. Confirm.
The family's lodging, the 'cachot', a former jail cell: confirm description.
Eighteen apparitions; spring uncovered at the ninth (February 25); name given March 25. Confirm.
Gascon wording 'Que soy era Immaculada Councepciou' as inscribed at the grotto; spelling varies in sources and the pronunciation guide is approximate. A Keeper or a Gascon speaker should check both.
Bernadette's remark that she was asked to tell, not to make people believe, is widely reported in varying wording; paraphrased.
Private revelation: CCC 67; the bishop of Tarbes approved the apparitions in 1862. Confirm.
Practice offers a Hail Mary 'if you pray'; no new prayer is written.
